subject.title: Session→model/runtime binding drift persists across doctor --fix --deep because the repair's provider-ownership registry is missing the literal id "openai"

question: Should literal `openai` auto session route state be owned by the OpenAI provider doctor contract, the Codex doctor contract, or a generic provider-state repair path?
rationale: The code-level fix is small, but `openai` is both the canonical OpenAI provider id and the provider id used by Codex app-server runs, so automation should not choose the permanent owner boundary on its own.

options.title: OpenAI owns canonical state
options.body: Add OpenAI-side doctor route-state ownership for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and keep Codex focused on Codex ids and legacy aliases.

options.title: Codex owns app-server OpenAI state
options.body: Add `openai` to the Codex doctor owner if maintainers consider OpenAI app-server route state Codex-owned for cleanup purposes.

options.title: Make auto fallback repair generic
options.body: Repair stale auto fallback overrides based on configured route mismatch without relying on provider-owner ids for this case.

recommendation.title: OpenAI owns canonical state
recommendation.body: Add OpenAI-side doctor route-state ownership for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and keep Codex focused on Codex ids and legacy aliases.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored and merged the closest prior doctor/Codex session-route repair work and is the clearest owner-boundary signal in history.
